## What to look for

- Where is the only active volcano? Why there?
- Follow one volcano as the plate carries it away: what does it become, step by step?
- In which direction does the plate move? On which side of the hotspot is the oldest island?
- The Pacific plate moves 7 to 10 cm a year over the Hawaiian hotspot. How far does it carry a volcano in 2.5 million years?
- Why does an island get lower as it moves away from the hotspot, even when it no longer erupts?

## How it works

The plume stays in place while the plate moves over it at a constant speed. A new volcano grows over the plume every 2.5 million years, then the plate carries it away: it stops erupting, is worn down by erosion and sinks with the plate, becoming an island, then an atoll ringed with coral and sand, then a seamount under the sea. Heights, distances and speeds are not to scale.
